analysis: Seed noise is tiny (baseline 5 seeds 0.326–0.334), so both round-1 gains are real. A deeper network (t00) and a success bonus of 5 on the cells reward (t01) did nothing. More optimisation per batch (t02: lr 0.001, 4 epochs) raised success to 0.56. Switching to iou_delta with bonus 5 and step penalty 0.01 (t03) raised it to 0.69. t01 shows the bonus alone does not help, so the gain comes from iou_delta and/or the step penalty. These two changes act on different things, optimisation and reward, so they will probably add up. Next round: combine them, push further on optimisation (more updates, higher lr), and run one ablation to find out whether the step penalty matters.

proposals.hypothesis: This combines t03's reward (iou_delta, bonus 5, step penalty 0.01) with t02's optimisation (lr 0.001, 4 epochs). The two gains should add up to dev success above 0.75. If the result is at or below 0.69, they do not stack.

Same as proposal 1, but with 8 minibatches, which doubles the gradient steps per rollout. This tests whether learning is still limited by the number of updates. If it does not beat proposal 1, 4x4 updates per batch is already enough.

Ablation: this is t03 with the step penalty removed. It isolates whether iou_delta alone drives the gain or whether the per-placement cost, which discourages extra bricks, matters. If success stays near 0.69, the penalty is irrelevant; if it falls clearly, keep the penalty and try 0.05 next.

Same as proposal 1, but with lr raised to 0.002. Learning rate was one of the two drivers of t02's gain, so pushing it further may help more under linear decay. If it falls below proposal 1 or becomes unstable, 0.001 is near the best value.

prompt:
## Task
An agent must build a target design in a small brick world.
- The world is a 5 x 5 base, up to 3 layers high. Bricks are one layer high with footprints 1x1, 1x2, 2x1 or 2x2.
- A placed brick drops until it rests on the highest filled cell under its footprint (or the ground), so overhangs with empty cells under them are possible and placement order matters.
- Each step the agent picks a brick type and an anchor cell, or DONE. An episode ends at DONE or after 17 placements. Bricks cannot be removed.
- Target designs are made by 3 to 8 random brick drops. Training uses a stream of fresh random designs; the held-out designs never appear in training.
- The agent observes the current build and the target as described by the obs_mode knob.

## Training and evaluation
- Each trial trains a PPO agent from scratch for exactly 524,288 environment steps on one CPU core. A trial that exceeds 600 seconds of wall-clock time is killed and counts as a failure (larger networks and more PPO epochs cost more time).
- After training, the agent runs greedily on 512 held-out dev designs. A build counts as a success when the project's checker says it matches the target design.
- Selection metric: dev success rate (higher is better). At the end, the trial with the highest dev success is selected. The selected recipe will then be retrained with new seeds and tested once on a separate hidden set of designs, so a lucky seed does not help.
- The baseline config was trained with 5 different seeds: dev success mean 0.330, min 0.326, max 0.334.

## Search space (every config must set every knob)
- lr: float, log-uniform in [0.0001, 0.003]. Adam learning rate.
- lr_schedule: one of ["constant", "linear_decay"]. Learning-rate schedule over the training budget.
- n_envs: one of [64, 128, 256, 512]. Parallel worlds per rollout.
- rollout_len: one of [8, 16, 32]. Steps per world per rollout (batch = n_envs x rollout_len).
- ppo_epochs: one of [1, 2, 4]. Passes over each rollout batch.
- n_minibatches: one of [2, 4, 8]. Minibatches per epoch.
- gamma: one of [0.9, 0.95, 0.99]. Discount factor.
- gae_lambda: one of [0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 1.0]. GAE lambda.
- clip_eps: one of [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]. PPO clipping range.
- ent_coef: float, log-uniform in [0.0001, 0.05]. Entropy bonus coefficient.
- vf_coef: one of [0.25, 0.5, 1.0]. Value-loss coefficient.
- max_grad_norm: one of [0.5, 1.0, 5.0]. Gradient-norm clip.
- adv_norm: one of [true, false]. Normalise advantages per minibatch.
- encoder: one of ["conv", "mlp"]. conv: fully convolutional, one logit per (brick type, anchor) cell; mlp: flattened grid into an MLP.
- width: one of [32, 64, 128]. Channels (conv) or hidden units (mlp).
- depth: one of [1, 2, 3, 4]. Number of conv or MLP layers.
- activation: one of ["relu", "gelu", "tanh"]. Activation function.
- norm: one of ["none", "layernorm"]. Normalisation after each layer.
- obs_mode: one of ["voxels", "heightmaps"]. voxels: every cell of the current build and the target, layer by layer; heightmaps: only the top-down height of each column (cheaper, smaller input).
- reward_mode: one of ["sparse", "cells", "iou_delta", "heightmap_delta"]. sparse: reward only for a finished build that matches; cells: +/- per placed cell inside/outside the target; iou_delta: change in voxel overlap (IoU) with the target; heightmap_delta: change in the share of columns whose height matches the target.
- success_bonus: one of [0.0, 1.0, 5.0]. Extra reward when the episode ends with the reward mode's notion of a match.
- step_penalty: one of [0.0, 0.01, 0.05]. Cost per placement.

## Baseline config
